title: Floor register: Positive-ink invoice
topics: Linked lists, binary trees and search trees
summary: Produce the sum of node values at each depth of the binary tree, starting with depth 0 at the root. Missing children contribute nothing. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.
descriptionMd:
The cabinet supervisor collects one total for every floor of a binary folder tree. Neri prepares an invoice that accepts only positive ink adjustments. Zero and negative derived readings stay off the invoice.

Produce the sum of node values at each depth of the binary tree, starting with depth 0 at the root. Missing children contribute nothing.

Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.

Implement floorRegisterPositiveInkInvoice(root, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Tree breadth-first traversal. Produce the sum of node values at each depth of the binary tree, starting with depth 0 at the root. Missing children contribute nothing. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 0 <= node count <= 31; JSON null placeholders do not count as nodes.
1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
Lists are acyclic. Trees use level-order JSON with null for missing children; [] is an empty root. The runner supplies nodes with val/next or val/left/right.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with tree breadth-first traversal. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

Produce the sum of node values at each depth of the binary tree, starting with depth 0 at the root. Missing children contribute nothing. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,-3,7]. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 14.
The derived sequence is [4,4,2]. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 10.
The derived sequence is []. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 0.
